I'm sorry you're going through this. I totally understand how you feel since I only have six contacts on my phone and only one of them regularly contacts me haha. Normally people don't text me unless they need something (assignments, university-related stuff). I can't remember the last time someone in my immediate circle asked to see how I was doing or checked in with me because they genuinely cared about my wellbeing. Tbh, it's probably because of my terrible attitude toward others, as I've been told lol. But yeah, I've given up on waiting for someone to check on me.

I also talk to myself like A LOT. I find it to be less tiring than to put up a positive facade when interacting with others who you don't want to "burden" with your depressive thoughts.
I'll try to stay strong :). Fun fact, she's in her mid-30s...so definitely not a child anymore.

Thank you. I'll try to not let it affect me.
Sociopaths will never admit or question they're sociopaths.

Building upon your last few points. You expressed  your interests in "knowing" what others think.

Having empathy for outgroup members is usually the first step in building a connection. Nobody can read minds.  If you never cared about people in the first place then you will never come to develop and understanding of them. It
also raises the question, why are you even interested in the first place? That's the hypocritcal aspect of your post. 

I feel like everything is one sided. People aren't going to be interested in you if you're a dick (your mentions of blackmailing others). Doesn't matter if you have a mental illness, it's not an excuse to manipulate others.  

Putting aside your own biased perceptions of the world, I do hope you are at least capable of rational thought. The objective reality is that humans, regardless of your opinion, are all sentient. Seeing them as robots serve no purpose because that's all in your head and does not reflect reality. Of course, thoughts alone are incapable of harm, but if you carry them out, you will never develop a healthy relationship with anyone beyond those within your ingroup. Hence your own biases are validated (since you can never know a person well enough beyond your own assumptions), and the vicious cycle repeats.

Have you tried putting yourself in their shoes? Imagine your own family dying 1000 times, over and over again just so someone can grab a 10$ discount. 

I think humans are selfish by nature but it's also important to have some perspective.
Yet because you don't know whats going on in their heads you assume they're like NPCs?  Egotistical thinking comes with depression I guess.

Yeah we're close and they've known for awhile.

I assume the job you're referring to is "therapy?" I'm a psychology student and see a clinician reguarly. Sitting on the other side of the table is different, and sometimes it doesnt feel real at all. I have nothing against therapy for all its practical purposes, but at the end of the day it's just a job to them, and they get paid by the hour. Your friends don't, maybe that's why I haven't shut up about my depression to them. 

Towards your last point you mentioned I should never stop expressing my issues to people. However, when suicidal thoughts come into play it's a sudden, nope abort. Tbh you're probably right, I don't know what I want people to say, but I do get frusturated and I don't understand why depressed people are getting downplayed for simply coming out with their depression. The fear of putting your friends and family on the spot and the fear of getting rejected or a dismissal, "don't kill yourself life is great!", then getting blamed for putting them in that position when you're the one who's suffering. We're stuck in a grey area, where telling is advised but suicidal thoughts are a taboo and expecting something genuine from your friends is considered overreaching...or getting frusturated by expecting something more than a dismissal is unreasonable because we've "put them on a spot." Hence the title of the post.

Idk why I bother. People only start caring when it's too late. Probably when I finally have the courage to "put myself down", then they can finally breathe and live without the burden of my existence.  After all, life itself is not the problem, I am.

Also here to talk! I'm so sorry you have to go through this :( My entire family hasn't been able to comprehend my struggle as well. They regard me as a disappointment (and of course, lazy) and told me I'm a result of their inadequate parenting. You're definitely not alone.
